title: Auli and Jim Corbett (Batch 7)
selection: Batch 7. Auli and Jim Corbett each had 4 sections. Adds who it's for, best time, practical info, safety (Auli), things to do (Corbett), FAQs and mistakes; fuller overviews as pending suggestions. Conflicts left out: Auli's height (2,800 m on Incredible India vs the 2,500–3,050 m range in AU1) and Shankaracharya's math 'just 6 km away'; Corbett's total reserve area (1,318.54 vs 1,288.31 sq km) and bird count (600+ vs 580); MUS_COR carries a conflict and is not used.

overview.text:
Auli — 'meadow' in Garhwali — is a slope of meadows between 2,500 and 3,050 m above Joshimath in Chamoli district, ringed by apple orchards and pine. Its 3-km run with a 500-m drop is India's best-known ski slope, run by GMVN; snow usually lies deep from January to March, the slopes are busiest from late November, and an artificial lake feeds snow-making in lean years.

The views reach Nanda Devi, Kamet, Dunagiri and Nilkanth. In summer Auli is the start of the Kuari Pass trek and walks to Gorson Bugyal, with campsites under the stars. Auli is 16 km above Joshimath by road, where the Alaknanda meets the Dhauliganga; Nandaprayag, one of the Panch Prayag, is nearby. Joshimath, the base town and gateway to Badrinath, is sinking along its ridge, so check local advisories before you go.

overview.text:
Jim Corbett National Park, set up in 1936, is India's first national park and the first under Project Tiger. Its 520.8 sq km of sal forest, river belts and grassland near Ramnagar shelter tigers, leopards, elephants, sambar and bears, along with some 580 bird species; Dhikala, with its old forest rest house, looks over the Patli Dun valley.

Safaris and forest stays are booked only on corbettgov.org. Dhikala opens about 15 November to 15 June and Bijrani about 15 October to 30 June, while Jhirna and Dhela stay open through the monsoon; April to mid-June gives the best chance of a tiger. Corbett's own home at Kaladhungi is now a museum. Pantnagar airport is about 120 km away, Nainital about 65 km.
